audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagrees with the already-audited mirror (aatrox__sylas), which reads Aatrox from Level 2 through First item and Sylas at Two+ items. Sylas's rows 1,2,3,5 read Skill and row 6 reads Aatrox.
audit.why: Both directions must state the same winner per row; mirror-fix.js overwrites disagreements. Win rate 47.72 over 658 games supports Aatrox owning the mid-lane stretch.
audit.corrected: Rows Level 2, Level 3, Levels 4-5 and First item read Aatrox; Two+ items reads Sylas. Level 6 left alone pending the question below.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text carries no real cooldown numbers; the packet flags zero sequencing cues in the whole entry.
audit.why: Umbral Dash (E) is 9/8/7/6/5s and Infernal Chains (W) is 20/18/16/14/12s — his escape and his hold are on very different clocks, and Sylas's W is 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s. Concrete numbers make the step-up advice actionable.
audit.corrected: Spike and wants text now name Umbral Dash's 5-9s window and Sylas's 9s W cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Deathbringer Stance's max-health heal and its auto-attack reset are never mentioned, and no anti-heal timing appears in the lane text.
audit.why: His sustain is the reason the 3-to-first-item stretch is his; Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade, and the passive's wind-up (not an ability cast) is the tell to step back.
audit.corrected: Spike and wants text now name Deathbringer Stance's max-health heal and call for early Grievous Wounds.

audit.why: Umbral Dash at 5-9s is the punishable window and is now stated as the hook cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: The missing-interactions file for Aatrox claims Infernal Chains (W) grounds Sylas's W and E.
audit.why: Riot's own W description says only that champions dragged back to the centre take damage again — no grounding is stated. The derived flag contradicts the description, so the claim is not asserted anywhere in this entry.
audit.corrected: No grounding claim written. Left as unknown.

edits.before: Aatrox's Q sweetspot knockups let him extend trades he should be losing; his passive healing turns every exchange in his favor unless you disengage first.
edits.after: Aatrox's Q knockups extend trades he should be losing, and Deathbringer Stance heals off your max health — buy Grievous Wounds early and leave before his third swing.

edits.before: Outlast your W cooldown with his passive healing stacking up on autos
edits.after: Stall past your 9s W cooldown while Deathbringer Stance heals off you

edits.before: Hook with E2 after he wastes a Q sweetspot, not into a loaded kit
edits.after: Hook E2 after Umbral Dash — it is down 5-9s and he cannot dash out

edits.before: Levels 4-5 cement Aatrox's extended-trade dominance; his passive healing on autos plus Q resets means staying in his face drains you faster than your W refills — fight in bursts only.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 cement Aatrox's extended-trade dominance: Deathbringer Stance heals off your max health and Umbral Dash returns every 6s, so he out-drains your 9s W — fight one rotation, then leave.

edits.before: At 2+ items Aatrox's stacked passive healing and Q damage fully outpace Riftmaker; play around objective pressure from your level-6 lead, not 1v1 dominance.
edits.after: At 2+ items you are the teamfight flex — a stolen ultimate plus Riftmaker sustain beats what Aatrox brings to a 5v5, so take fights near objectives, never in his sidelane.
